Proxy ruling under the maintainer's delegation quoted above (carried into this project by its owner's standing rule 「卡线程报 needs_decision 时，另开 fable 裁决线程，有把握就裁并把裁决落在 GitHub 上，没把握才给 Bill 发决策卡」), by the review thread's session `session_01APSsvEvjFUTm2kWZj3s6Zp` ([project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuMq9R419AHnf4qjyJKgmmcN)), on the `domain:services` seat 1 card thread's needs_decision fork (claim `6347648881`, report `6348691318`, session `session_01Mnj4nkWuhJ18xEdZvb2cjE`, draft PR #25270 at `45536612`). Marker: `auto-adjudicated`. ⚠️ Reversible on one word from the maintainer; nothing here forecloses that.

## The question

Slice 1 of the `engine.ts` split moves the eight registration-time checks of `AutomationEngine` to `src/flow-registration-checks.ts`, move-only, by #23050's shape B. The published `dist/index.d.ts` (and the identical `index.d.cts`) of `@objectstack/service-automation` is not byte-identical to base: 18 lines differ, every one the same string-literal union printed with two members swapped (`"summary" | "record"` ↔ `"record" | "summary"` on 9 lines; `"package" | "artifact" | "env-forced"` ↔ `"artifact" | "package" | "env-forced"` on 9 lines). After sorting the members of string-literal unions both sides hash the same; the ESM and CJS export lists are identical (39 names); no declaration is added, removed, renamed or retyped, and no private member becomes public or protected. The cause, measured by the dev with an instrumented TypeScript 6.0.3 checker on tsup's DTS program: TypeScript prints a union's members in the order their literal types were created, and the DTS build checks files in program order, where an imported module precedes its importer, so the moved bodies (which name `FlowParsed`) are now checked before all of `engine.ts`. Every later cut that `engine.ts` imports does the same. The claim `6347648881` had said 「⛔ The published `.d.ts` of `@objectstack/service-automation` does not change … If no move-only shape keeps it, this thread stops and returns `needs_decision`」, so the thread stopped. The forks:

- **A** (the card thread's recommendation) — the series' `.d.ts` bar is identity after sorting string-literal union members, plus the same export list; each slice reports raw and normalised hashes; `skip-changeset` stays, as on #23050's slices.
- **B** — any byte change is a published change: a `patch` changeset per slice (about ten "internal refactor" releases no consumer can observe) and `skip-changeset` removed here.
- **C** — stop the series and keep `engine.ts` whole.

## This thread's re-measure

Rebuilt in this thread's container from a fresh `pnpm install` and `turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/service-automation...'` at base `cc8d886` (the PR's base), then the package alone with the PR head's three source files (`45536612`) checked out:

- raw `dist/index.d.ts` = `index.d.cts`: base sha256 `fa59fa6b2b0b0e44709a3720e0fc8e66b2ed2d100277e57410ca9f020eb44158`, head `061f950a0047c61b0e747dcfefb44c64bdf4c21150faafb72364d1a2350f965b` — the dev's two readings, reproduced.
- `diff base head`: 18 line pairs (36 diff lines), each pair the same line with two members of one string-literal union swapped: 9 × `_lockSource?: "package" | "artifact" | "env-forced" | undefined` ↔ `"artifact" | "package" | …`; 9 × the field-type union with `"summary" | "record"` ↔ `"record" | "summary"` (6 on `type:`, 3 on `type?:`). No other line differs.
- normalised (members of every string-literal union run sorted in place, nothing else touched; the one-liner below): base and head both `bb7fefdc30c19ebb1dac308eeb00418a79c8465b9409f511f66c56cf7d398cd5`, `cmp` silent — the dev's normalised hash, reproduced.
- positive control: the head `.d.ts` with one declaration changed in kind (`private registrationChecks;` → `registrationChecks;`, line 4453) normalises to `7a323d3459b9e40cde2b312d618bc46c17bd1eb2322433874702e6c670038ca3` ≠ `bb7fefdc…`: the normaliser does not hide a visibility change.
- export lists at head: ESM 39 names, CJS 39 names (the dev's reading; base not re-counted here, the report's 39 = 39 stands).
- the normaliser used (so the seat reruns it from the same two files): `node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8");process.stdout.write(s.replace(/"[^"\n]*"(?:\s*\|\s*"[^"\n]*")+/g,r=>r.split(/\s*\|\s*/).sort().join(" | ")))' dist/index.d.ts | sha256sum`.
- the dev's cause (literal-type creation order under program order) is not re-instrumented here; it is consistent with the diff's shape (the two swapped literals are exactly the ones the moved bodies' `FlowParsed` signatures reach first) and is marked **unverified by this thread** as a mechanism; the ruling rests on the measured diff, not on the mechanism.

## Governing text, read at `origin/main` `cc8d886` (the PR's base)

- The card's ask 1 「Each slice is **move-only**: no logic changes」, ask 3 「Every slice proves it moved nothing」, ask 5 「⛔ No new gate」; the maintainer's words it carries out, #24586 `6270097840`: 「24586 同意A，是否建议这波分拆等 v18 发布之后再处理。」 The maintainer's terms for the parent series #23050, as `6205442867` quotes them: 「每片只搬代码、路由表前后一致」. Neither names the `.d.ts`.
- Where the `.d.ts` bar comes from: #23050 slice 1's claim `6134225153` (a seat's dispatch line, not the maintainer's), 「⛔ The published `.d.ts` of `@objectstack/rest` does not change: no private member becomes public or protected on `RestServer`. If no move-only shape keeps it, stop and return `needs_decision`.」 The sentence states its own purpose: member visibility. This card's claim `6347648881` and #25224's claim `6347670835` (「the proof owed is `@objectstack/plugin-auth`'s `dist/*.d.ts` byte-identical to base and the same export list」) repeat it.
- AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist step 3: 「A bug fix in a released package takes a **`patch`** changeset — never none, and ⛔ never `skip-changeset`: that label is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package.」 The label's own description: 「PR has no user-facing published change; bypasses the changeset gate」. AGENTS.md's `CHANGELOG.md` row: it 「ships inside the npm tarball as the text an upgrading agent greps」.
- Precedent: #23050's twelve slices (PR #23116 through #24205) all moved bundle bytes and carried `skip-changeset`; the repo reads 「publishes nothing」 as no observable published change, not as a byte-identical tarball.
- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` 〈升级与决策〉: 「具名不升级类(立即行动):恢复不变量;技术任务间顺序与依赖;验证策略;说明书脱节。」; 「dev 的 `needs_decision` 经 PM 复核落进不升级类的,PM 直接答复不上传。」; 「① 静默丢弃的声明并入既有拒收集;新支复用母单裁决直接入队,真实语义差异才重开。」; 「**新增门禁默认否**」. `references/review-checklist.md`: 「引 entry `.d.ts` 逐字节相同的读数必须同块带阳性对照,它只判名字集。」

## Ruling: A

This is a verification-strategy question, a named no-escalation class: the bar under dispute is a seat's proof criterion, written as a proxy for 「no private member becomes public or protected」, and the proxy has met a TypeScript printer artefact its author did not foresee. No floor moves: union member order has no meaning to any consumer (assignability, narrowing and inference are unchanged), the declaration set is the same, the export set is the same, no gate is loosened and none is added. The PM answers it here; it does not go up.

**Why not B.** A changeset is 「the text an upgrading agent greps」; a `patch` entry that can only say 「internal refactor」 gives that reader a release with nothing in it, ten times over the series, and the same again on #25223 and #25224. The base order is itself an accident of which `engine.ts` line first touches each literal, so any ordinary edit of the file could flip it without a changeset either; tying the series to it ties it to the accident, not to the contract.

**Why not C.** The maintainer ordered the split (「同意A」, restart condition read true in `6291735609`); the obstacle is a printer artefact, not a contract. C loses the card's goal for nothing a consumer could observe.

Fixed here, so no slice of this series opens a second decision on the same point:

1. **The series' `.d.ts` bar** (this card, and by 元判据① the sibling restart-act cards #25223 and #25224, which carry the same dispatch line): a cut's published `.d.ts` (`index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`, each) must (a) keep the same declaration set, with no private member made public or protected and nothing added, removed, renamed or retyped; (b) be byte-identical to base after exactly one normalisation, sorting the members of each string-literal union in place (the `"a" | "b"` sequences; nothing else is normalised: no whitespace, no comments, no reordering of declarations, no widening of the normaliser later); (c) keep the ESM and CJS export lists identical to base; (d) account for every raw-diff line as a union-member-order swap: the report states the raw diff's line count and that the diff of the two normalised files is empty, so each differing line pair is the same line with union members permuted. Any residual after (b), or any diff of another kind (a blank line, an inlined alias, a moved declaration — #23050 slice 1 met one, `6135442258`), is outside this ruling: stop and report the fork, ⛔ do not widen the normaliser and ⛔ do not add a changeset to pass.
2. **What each report carries, in one block**: the raw sha256 of base and head, the normalised sha256 of base and head, the normaliser command verbatim (one shell or node one-liner the seat reruns from the same two files), the raw-diff line count, and the positive control the review checklist requires for a byte-identical reading: the same normaliser applied to the head `.d.ts` with one injected change of kind (a) (a private member made public, or a renamed member) yields a different normalised hash. A block without the control reads INCONCLUSIVE, as the checklist says.
3. **Not a gate.** The normaliser is a report reading the seat reruns at ACCEPT, in the report and the PR body only; ⛔ no `scripts/` file, no CI step, no `check:` script (card ask 5; 「新增门禁默认否」).
4. **`skip-changeset` stays** on every cut that meets item 1; ⛔ no `patch` changeset for a union-order diff. A cut that fails item 1 does not take a changeset either: it stops (item 1).
5. **The claim lines** 「the published `.d.ts` does not change」 (this card) and 「`dist/*.d.ts` byte-identical to base」 (#25224) read, from this comment on, as item 1. The next slice's claim on each card spells item 1 out instead of the byte-identity wording; the current claims are not re-posted.
6. **Premise, falsifiable, this cut:** the raw diff at the final head is union-member-order only, and the dev's cause (program order, literal creation order) is the one the re-measure above reads. A later head whose raw diff carries any other line falsifies it: stop and report, ⛔ do not hard-pass.

### Why A, on the four axes (business standpoint)

- **① Long-term soundness (weight ≥50%).** Two years out the platform's move-only proof for a split is a contract reading, not a printer reading: the same declarations, the same visibility, the same exports. A keeps that bar strict on every byte that carries meaning and names the one byte class that carries none. B makes the release record say something false by omission (a release with no change) and C abandons an ordered decomposition over an artefact.
- **② Measured business pull.** Zero consumers can observe union member order (type-level only; no runtime, no `.d.ts` reader in the repo keys on it: `check:api-surface` reads `packages/spec/dist`, not this package). The pull is the maintainer's split order, in flight on three cards.
- **③ AI-error prevention.** An agent that moves a member and lets it become public, renames it, or drops a declaration still fails loudly: items 1(a), 1(d) and the positive control catch it, and the report must show the control. Under A the normaliser cannot hide a real change because it touches only union member order and every other byte must match.
- **④ Startup no-sprawl.** No new gate, no script, no changeset noise; one report block per cut. B adds about thirty empty patch releases across the three cards; C spends the ordered work for nothing.

Only-① pick: A. Do ②③④ flip it: no. Effort for the chosen letter: none beyond the report block on PR #25270; the seat's ACCEPT proceeds.

The PR body's 「stays a draft until one question is ruled」 is answered here; the dev leaves the body as written (one write at `pr_create`) and the seat reads the ruling and the report block. `skip-changeset` stays. - Slice 2 of this card, and cut 1 of #25224 and the first cut of #25223 when dispatched, apply item 1 directly and cite this comment with `Ruling-ref:`; a raw diff of any other kind is a fresh fork on that card, not covered here.
